n: The people of Kirjath-jearim bring the ark to Abinadab's hilltop house and set apart his son Eleazar to guard it. It would remain there until David brought it to Jerusalem.

f.g: set apart, consecrated for a holy task

n: Twenty years pass with the ark sidelined. During this time Israel begins to mourn and long for the Lord — a sign that hearts are softening toward repentance.

f.g: mourned and longed for the Lord

n: Samuel calls for wholehearted repentance: get rid of foreign idols, prepare your hearts, and serve the Lord alone. Then God will deliver you. True repentance is shown by actions.

f.g: Plural of Ashtoreth (Astarte), a Canaanite fertility goddess.

n: Israel obeys, removing their Baal and Ashtoreth idols and worshipping the Lord alone.

f.g: Plural of Baal, the Canaanite storm and fertility god, worshipped in many local forms.

n: Samuel gathers the nation to Mizpeh and promises to pray for them. A prophet's intercession for his people is a recurring role in scripture.

f.g: “Watchtower,” a town in Benjamin's territory north of Jerusalem, used as a gathering place.

n: The people pour out water before the Lord, fast, and confess their sins. Pouring water may symbolize hearts poured out in sorrow. Samuel acts as judge and leader.

f.w: poured it out before the LORD
We have sinned against the LORD

n: The Philistines see Israel's gathering as a military threat and advance to attack. Israel, gathered for worship and not war, is frightened.
This time Israel does not reach for the ark as a charm; they ask Samuel to keep praying for them. Their trust has shifted to the Lord Himself.

f.w: Cease not to cry unto the LORD

n: Samuel offers a young lamb as a whole burnt offering and pleads for Israel, and the Lord answers. The lamb points ahead to Jesus Christ, the Lamb of God.
As the Philistines charge, the Lord thunders against them, throwing them into confusion and defeat. The battle is won by God, not by Israel's weapons.
Israel's soldiers chase the fleeing Philistines as far as Beth-car, completing the victory.

f.g: A place west of Mizpeh whose exact location is unknown.

n: Samuel sets up a memorial stone named Eben-ezer, “stone of help,” declaring, “Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.” The place of earlier defeat becomes a monument to God's help.
The Philistines are subdued and stop invading during Samuel's leadership. Faithfulness brought the protection the ark alone could not.
Israel recovers the towns the Philistines had taken, and there is peace with the Amorites, a general name for other Canaanite peoples.

f.g: Here a broad term for the native peoples of Canaan.

n: Samuel serves as Israel's judge for the rest of his life — the last of the judges and the first of a new line of great prophets.
He travels a yearly circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpeh to settle disputes and lead the people — a traveling judge and spiritual leader.
Samuel's home base is Ramah, where he also judges and builds an altar to the Lord. With the tabernacle at Shiloh apparently disrupted, worship took place at other sites.
